title: Noticing Parts of Your Body
summary: A slow body scan with the breath: forehead, jaw, chest, thigh, calf and more.
script:
Welcome. This is your time. Your time to relax, and your time to breathe.

Find a comfortable position. You can sit, or you can lie down. Just make sure your body feels supported.

If you want, you can close your eyes. Or you can keep them softly open, looking down.

There is nothing to do right now. Nothing to fix. Nothing to solve. Just be here, in this moment, with your breath.

Let your body settle. Feel the surface beneath you. Notice how it supports your weight. Let your shoulders soften. Let your hands rest. Let your whole body feel heavy and calm.

Take a slow breath in… and let it out slowly.

Again. Breathe in… and breathe out.

There are two words I'd like you to notice, right here, in this quiet moment.

The first word is inhale. To inhale means to breathe in, to bring air softly into your body.

The second word is exhale. To exhale means to breathe out, to let that air gently leave.

Inhale is the movement of taking in. Exhale is the movement of letting go. Inhale and Exhale are verbs.

Notice your next inhale. Feel the air entering, cool and light. Notice your next exhale. Feeling the air leaving, soft and warm.

Today, we are going to relax the whole body, using these two movements as a gentle guide.

Bring your attention to the top of your head. Take a slow inhale, and imagine the breath rising gently to meet it.

Now exhale, feeling any tightness there simply melt away, like it's floating off with the air.

Move to your forehead. Inhale, bring your awareness there. Exhale, and let it smooth completely.

Notice your eyes. Inhale gently. Exhale, and let your eyelids grow heavier, softer.

Bring attention to your jaw. This is a place that often holds tension without us noticing. Inhale slowly. Exhale, and let your jaw loosen, unlocked and calm.

Let your lips part slightly, without effort. Your whole body now feels still. Peaceful.

Move to your neck. Inhale. Exhale, and feel the muscles there lengthen and soften.

Now your shoulders. Inhale, and notice them rise just slightly. Exhale, and let them drop, away from your ears, releasing everything they've been holding.

Move into your arms. Inhale, sending your awareness down to your elbows. Exhale, and feel your arms grow heavy, resting completely.

Your hands, your fingers. Inhale, notice them fully. Exhale, and let them soften, doing nothing at all.

Bring your awareness to your chest. Notice something simple here. When you inhale, your chest rises gently. When you exhale, your chest falls gently.

Inhale… rise. Exhale… fall. This has been happening quietly, your whole life, without your help.

Stay here a moment, simply watching. Inhale. Exhale. Rise. Fall.

Let this same rhythm move further down your body.

Inhale, bring awareness to your stomach. Exhale, and let it soften completely.

Move into your back. Inhale, noticing your upper back. Exhale, to feel it widen slightly, more relaxed than before.

Bring your breath into your lower back. Inhale gently. Exhale, and let this area grow soft.

Now your hips. Inhale, and simply notice them. Exhale, and let them feel wide and supported.

Move into your thighs. Inhale. Exhale, and let them grow heavy, sinking into the surface beneath you.

Past your knees, into your calves. Inhale slowly. Exhale, and feel any tightness disappear.

Finally, your ankles, and your feet. Inhale, sending your awareness all the way down. Exhale, and let your toes soften, one by one.

Notice your whole body now. From your head to your feet, every part has softened, just a little more, with every inhale, and every exhale.

Stay here for a moment, simply noticing this rhythm continue on its own. Inhale. Exhale. Calm. Steady.

Let these gentle words settle into your mind, matching your breath.

Inhale calm.

Exhale tension.

Inhale peace.

Exhale everything you no longer need.

Take a few more slow breaths, and let these words become part of you.

Notice, one more time, this deep sense of calm spreading through your whole body. Every inhale brings softness. Every exhale releasing what's no longer needed.

Now, slowly, bring your attention back to the room around you. Notice the surface beneath you again. Notice your breath, still soft and slow.

Gently move your fingers. Gently move your toes. Let your body slowly wake up, feeling relaxed and calm.

Take one more slow inhale… and let your exhale be long and gentle.

When you are ready, softly open your eyes.

Carry this calm with you. Carry this deep sense of rest with you, into the rest of your day.

You are calm. You are safe. And you are exactly where you need to be.

vocabulary.definition: the flat part of your face above your eyebrows and below your hair
the part of your leg above the knee
the part of your leg behind your shin, below the knee
the joint that connects your foot to your leg
the part of your body where your leg connects to your torso, on the side
